A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-JEM work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation benchmarks, guidance demonstrations, adversarial robustness experiments and architecture/objective ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments and qualitative demonstrations, including the appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Both retain the joint-energy and adversarial objectives, vision-encoder training, AdamW sampling and Algorithm 1. v2 adds an objective equation, but describes no accompanying revision to the algorithm, architecture or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain DataComp training, MS-COCO generation, T2I-CompBench compositionality, TEdBench metric evaluation, diffusion guidance and the same CLIPDraw/VQGAN+CLIP scenarios. No new evaluated dataset or task is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the guidance demonstrations. Table 2 abbreviates Stable Diffusion names without replacing methods. Newly discussed DiffusionCLIP and BLIP3-o are not added to evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Both report 20,000 training steps, 50 generation steps, 30,000 MS-COCO samples, ten samples per CompBench prompt and the same metrics and attack budget. Table 4 settings are unchanged; newly disclosed hardware and training duration are documentation additions.

E4.justification: The architecture and objective ablations, adversarial and noise-sensitivity tests, augmentation comparisons and stochasticity examples are retained. Appendix H discusses existing evidence rather than adding a diversity or noise-sensitivity experiment.

E5.justification: Existing sample averaging and same-seed diffusion illustrations are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Benchmark and sampling-resource tables retain their values, and qualitative result images are unchanged. For example, CLIP-JEM-XXL retains FID 23.4 in Table 1 and CompBench average 0.4000 in Table 2. Figure merging and renumbering introduce no new results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds Equation 5, an explicit minimax objective using one minus cosine similarity and optimization over both encoder parameter sets. The joint-energy definitions and Appendix E's SGLD/Taylor derivation remain unchanged. No new proof or theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: multimodal joint-energy modeling, direct image generation, improved guidance and a more robust evaluation metric. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix H explicitly acknowledges limited sample diversity and links it to small injected noise chosen for stability. Its spatial-compositionality limitation was already discussed in v1. Appendix G adds an explicit non-state-of-the-art FID qualification and a probabilistic-ranking interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly reports training on eight A40 GPUs and ten days for 20,000 ConvNext-XXL iterations. Pretrained checkpoints, hyperparameters, sampling-resource measurements and the promised code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix G expands comparisons with diffusion generators and systems using CLIP image encoders, adding DiffusionCLIP and BLIP3-o citations. It elaborates the existing positioning of CLIP-JEM as generating directly from CLIP without a separate generative backbone.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include expanded EBM explanation in Section 2.1, new appendix sections G–H, corrected table cross-references, abbreviated baseline names and publication/author information.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a predominantly single-column journal layout, substantially redistributing figures, tables and algorithms. v1 Figures 5 and 6 become panels of v2 Figure 5; captions and table placement are reformatted throughout while their evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: Training-resource disclosure and the explicit diversity limitation improve transparency. However, new Equation 5 uses a cosine-only objective over both encoders, conflicting with the retained contrastive ClipLoss and frozen-text protocol. Appendix G also describes energy as proportional to likelihood, contrary to Equation 4's exponential relationship. With empirical evidence unchanged, these documentation gains and new mathematical inconsistencies leave the net quality effect uncertain.
